subjective: The pet parent reports that the kittens are not fighting but one kitten occasionally bites the other without using claws or nails. The kittens remain calm when left alone for a few hours. No gut issues or abnormal defecation have been noticed. The mother and sister of the kitten passed away 15 days ago. The vaccination status of one kitten is not updated; only deworming was done before adoption about four months ago. The pet parent adopted the kitten five months ago.
objective: No physical examination findings or vital signs were documented during the consultation. The veterinarian noted that the kittens are calm and not aggressive despite occasional biting without claws. No gut or gastrointestinal abnormalities were observed or reported.
assessment: The kittens are generally healthy with no signs of gastrointestinal issues or aggression. Vaccination status is incomplete for one kitten, requiring update. Deworming schedule needs to be maintained according to age and weight. Occasional biting without claws is not causing harm and is considered normal behavior.
plan: 1. Continue deworming every 15 days until the kitten reaches 3 months of age, then monthly until 6 months. 2. Administer combined vaccination including two vaccines and rabies vaccine as soon as possible. 3. Repeat deworming next month. 4. Provide separate food bowls to prevent feeding issues. 5. Monitor for post-vaccination reactions such as fever, dullness, or reduced appetite; these usually resolve within 24 to 48 hours. 6. Vaccinate when the pet is healthy and not under stress, especially during heat cycles. 7. Schedule and plan the next booster vaccination after review. 8. Pet parent to report any signs or concerns promptly.
conclusion: The kittens are currently healthy with no signs of gastrointestinal or behavioral problems despite occasional non-aggressive biting. Deworming and vaccination schedules require updating, with vaccination planned to be administered soon. Post-vaccination monitoring is advised. Separate feeding arrangements are recommended to ensure proper nutrition. Follow-up and booster vaccinations will be planned after assessment. The pet parent is advised to observe and report any changes or concerns.
key_issues: 1. Incomplete vaccination status requiring update and booster planning. 2. Deworming schedule adherence based on age and weight. 3. Behavioral observation of occasional non-aggressive biting between kittens. 4. Feeding behavior requiring separate food bowls to prevent competition.
abnormal_findings: No abnormal findings reported or observed during the consultation.
customer_instructions: 1. Administer deworming every 15 days until 3 months of age, then monthly until 6 months. 2. Vaccinate the kitten with the combined vaccine including rabies as soon as possible. 3. Provide separate food bowls for each kitten. 4. Monitor for any post-vaccination reactions such as fever, dullness, or reduced appetite, which typically resolve within 24 to 48 hours. 5. Vaccinate only when the kitten is healthy and not stressed, especially avoiding vaccination during heat if possible. 6. Report any signs or concerns to the veterinarian promptly. 7. Plan for booster vaccinations after initial vaccination.
reminders: 1. Repeat deworming next month. 2. Schedule and administer combined vaccination as soon as possible. 3. Plan and schedule booster vaccinations after initial vaccination. 4. Monitor for post-vaccination reactions for 24 to 48 hours. 5. Follow up on any behavioral or health concerns.
